set.body:
Defect: D8 (four part-offset maps, one name, two incompatible semantics: score.py:37 and matched.py:14 use media-part-b 100000.0 -- an order-preserving SENTINEL, correct, since both feed only Kendall tau-b; agreement.py:28 uses the real 1426.0 because it measures gaps; filmfest_gold_film.py:23 adds a fourth in a fourth key space -- and NOTHING declares which is which) + D9 (run1EndRow 482 at sherlock.scala:66 vs PART_A_LAST_ROW 481 at extract_scene_frames.py:48: one fact, two languages, two conventions) + D10 (adding a corpus means forking a runner: run-filmfestival.py IS the fork of run-arm.sh).

Do: corpus-intake emits storymodel4s.corpus.descriptor/v1: clocks, clock maps, participant lists and exclusions, id patterns, gold granularity and coverage. tools/recall-study/ scorers read it. run-arm.sh takes a corpus id. THE IN-TREE PRECEDENT IS agreement.py:31-45, which ALREADY reads parts.json and falls back to a literal only if absent -- the only data-driven seam in the tree, and it is the judge of record. Generalize that rather than inventing a mechanism. The two senses of 'part offset' become two DECLARED records and the ambiguity stops being representable.

Tests: Python tests under tools/recall-study/tests/ drive each scorer from a synthetic descriptor and assert the Sherlock numbers are UNCHANGED. Descriptor round-trip test in Scala.

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): change a descriptor offset -> scorer output must change. Delete the descriptor -> the scorer must refuse BY NAME, not fall back to a default.

Exit: No corpus constant remains in tools/recall-study/*.py or run-arm.sh -- verified by grep, recorded in the commit body. The grep must also catch extract_scene_frames.py:50, which hardcodes an absolute path into a .worktrees/perception-first-court checkout that may not exist.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S3, P6
set.title: intake P6: emit a corpus descriptor and delete the corpus constants from Python/shell
